summary.headline: Varroc Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33.6% YoY to INR29,479 mn, but EBITDA margin eased to 8.9% (9.1% a year ago) on unrecovered war-related inflation.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 33.6% YoY and 11.9% QoQ, with India up 29.5% and overseas up 104.1%. EBITDA margin was 8.9%, up from 8.5% in Q1 but below 9.1% in Q2 FY26, as war-related input cost recoveries from customers lagged. Q2 PBT before JV and exceptional items was INR1,401 mn (4.7% of revenue), and reported PBT of about INR78 crore was hit by exceptional items linked to the Italy lighting restructuring and a tax dispute. Net debt rose to INR5,547 mn from INR4,952 mn in March 2026, driven by capex and about INR1,140 mn of agreed but uncollected recoveries in H1.

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Revenue +29.5% YoY in Q2 and +29.1% in H1. India EBITDA margin was about 10.3% in Q2 vs about 10.6% in Q1 and 11.5% a year ago, per analyst figures that management did not dispute, mainly due to war-related under-recovery.

segments.name: Overseas business
segments.commentary: Revenue +104.1% YoY in Q2 (management cited about 138% in the opening remarks) and +70.7% in H1. Overseas profitability is still weak, with Romania targeted to reach EBITDA break-even by year-end and R&D spend continuing.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: Bajaj about 46% of total revenue; overseas about 13%; two-wheeler and three-wheeler about 75% of revenue.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Opened FY27 at INR13,509 crore; added over INR1,000 crore in H1 and executed INR823 crore, leaving about INR3,700 crore at end-H1. EV orders are 48% and Bajaj 55% of order intake.

guidance_outlook: If macro conditions do not worsen, India EBITDA margin should return to last year's levels by end-FY27 and strengthen further in FY28 (management said it does not usually guide).
FY27 full-year capex maintained at INR500-550 crore; about INR300+ crore spent in H1, leaving about INR200+ crore for H2.
Net debt expected to stay around current levels through FY27 (plus or minus) and fall significantly only by end-FY28.
Net new order wins target of about INR2,500 crore annualised peak revenue for FY27 (internal target, not guidance), against about INR1,013 crore in H1.

Forsee Power India: management targets at least INR1,000 crore revenue over the next two to three years; overseas annualised revenue target of INR2,500 crore-plus this year was stated in the Forsee context.
Italy two-wheeler lighting restructuring to be completed in about six months; benefits flow from FY28, with a three-year payback on one-time shutdown costs.
Thailand four-wheeler lighting plant to start production mid-2027.
Management expects the war-related recovery pressure to moderate in Q3 and Q4 as recoveries flow through.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR500-550 crore; about INR300+ crore spent in H1 FY27, leaving about INR200+ crore for H2.

Forsee Power India: Varroc to take a controlling 45% stake with an option to add 6% more; expected to be consolidated as a subsidiary once SHA/SSA conclude. Management said there is no current plan to go beyond this.
Italy two-wheeler lighting manufacturing to be moved to Romania and Vietnam; restructuring to be completed in about six months.
Thailand four-wheeler lighting plant to start production in mid-2027.
Traction motor supply to a second Bajaj-linked customer was expected to start earlier; management said it is very close after a late-stage alignment issue on the customer side.
demand_pricing: Industry volumes in Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26: two-wheelers +16.3%, three-wheelers +23.7%, passenger vehicles +24.9%, commercial vehicles +33.9%; electric two-wheelers +115%.
Management said 5-6% of revenue growth came from commodity pass-through; the rest was volume.
Aftermarket growth slowed to about 10% YoY in Q2 vs a historical 25-35%; management said Q1 was hit by war-related issues, Q2 recovered, and new aftermarket products were added.

Two-wheeler lighting revenue dipped in Q2 due to a seasonal August shutdown at European customers (Piaggio); management said there is no de-growth and new overseas two-wheeler lighting business has been won.

Recovery of war-related cost is not automatic. It depends on firm customer confirmation during this period, and the company recognises it only after agreement, though underlying contracts often provide for it.
Management said it is not seeing a major market share gain in lighting; growth tracked industry volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India EBITDA margin fall QoQ while consolidated margin rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed India softness to war-related under-recoveries, which it called short-term, plus business mix shifts toward EV. It expects operating leverage to help once recoveries come through.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Romania business reach break-even, and when will overseas losses ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Romania internal target is EBITDA break-even by year-end. R&D spend will not change materially. Performance should improve from Q4, with most benefit in FY28. Q2 Romania electronics number included design income, so it should not be used as a run rate.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR114 crore pending recovery will hit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Under-recovery is about 0.6-0.8% of margin YoY. The INR114 crore is agreed price revision awaiting cash collection, so it is a cash-flow item. Management expects it to be recovered in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the arbitration with OPmobility and the TYC case have a financial impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to close both cases before FY27 year-end. The CFO said there is a claim and a counterclaim of similar size and no financial direction can be given. No provision was made in Q2 for these disputes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Forsee Power revenue potential and battery pack market size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least INR1,000 crore revenue over the next two to three years. Market size is about INR35,000-50,000 per two-wheeler pack, roughly double for three-wheelers, multiplied by EV penetration. Forsee revenue is currently low.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex and net debt guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. FY27 capex is INR500-550 crore. Net debt will be around current levels this year and should fall significantly by end-FY28, helped by government incentives and customer recoveries.

risks_watch: Under-recovery of war-related commodity and electronics inflation (about 0.6-0.8% margin impact) and the INR114-115 crore of agreed but uncollected recoveries.
Overseas EBITDA losses (Romania, R&D) persist; the break-even target is by year-end.
OPmobility ICC arbitration (claim of USD66.4 million) and the TYC Singapore case, with a targeted resolution before FY27 year-end.
Italy restructuring one-time costs and exceptional items; benefits begin FY28.
Forsee Power acquisition closure and consolidation; the revenue ramp depends on execution.
Aftermarket growth slowdown (about 10% in Q2) and whether it recovers.
Delayed traction motor supply start to a second Bajaj-linked customer.
Management said Q3 demand could moderate after the festive season, but it expects the momentum to continue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and EV growth, but cautious on margins, which management ties to war-related recoveries that have not yet been realised. Management was evasive on Forsee valuation, battery-pack margins, and the timing of the traction motor start.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA for quarter two of FY 2027 was INR2,611 million, representing an EBITDA margin of 8.9% compared with 8.5% in quarter one of FY 2027 and 9.1% in quarter two of FY 2026.
We will continue to focus on recovering commodity inflation, improving contribution margins, increasing productivity, and maintaining a discipline on fixed costs.
Our net debt-to-equity ratio remained at a comfortable 0.29, while our net debt to an annualized adjusted EBITDA stood at 0.57x, at the end of September 2026.
Definitely it should come down from the current levels by end of next year. This year it will more or less be around these levels, plus or minus.

adds.what: Italy two-wheeler lighting production moved to Romania and Vietnam (restructuring, ~6 months to complete)

growth.why: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 33.6% YoY, with management attributing 5-6% to commodity pass-through and the rest to volume; FY27 capex of INR500-550 crore is held with about INR300+ crore spent in H1, and the India EBITDA margin is guided back to last-year levels by end-FY27, though recoveries of war-related costs remain unconfirmed and no FY27 revenue growth number is given.
